claim: Use Quality-Calibrated QCR as the main paper-facing method family.
evidence: Stage 16-B recommends `Quality-Calibrated QCR with adaptive consistency refinement`. Primary adaptive-minus-quality mean delta is +0.0004 AUROC.

claim: Candidate quality calibration is the main effective component.
evidence: Primary quality-minus-naive mean delta is +0.0096 AUROC; all-protocol quality-minus-naive mean delta is +0.0365 AUROC.

claim: Adaptive consistency is a conservative refinement, not the main source of improvement.
evidence: Primary adaptive-minus-quality mean delta is only +0.0004 AUROC; all-protocol adaptive-minus-quality mean delta is +0.0006 AUROC.

claim: Do not claim fixed quality-consistency fusion as the final method.
evidence: Primary fixed-QC-minus-quality mean delta is +0.0043 AUROC, but earlier robustness checks showed fixed consistency is not stable across protocols.

claim: Do not claim consistency is universally beneficial.
evidence: Fixed consistency was not robust across all protocols, and adaptive consistency only gives a small safe bonus.

claim: Localization-guided VLM evidence becomes more reliable when crop evidence is calibrated by candidate quality.
evidence: Primary quality-minus-naive mean delta is +0.0096 AUROC with win rate 1.0000.

claim: Adaptive consistency can be retained as a reliability-gated refinement that avoids overcommitting to unstable fixed consistency.
evidence: Primary adaptive-minus-fixed-QC mean delta is -0.0039 AUROC; all-protocol adaptive-minus-fixed-QC mean delta is +0.0099 AUROC.

claim: Use Quality-Calibrated QCR as the main method; describe adaptive consistency as a small gated refinement.
evidence: This recommendation comes from Stage 16-B paper-facing comparison.
